title: The Language Update
notes: Choose the app's language: 18 languages, most spoken first, including Bulgarian. On Windows, Mac and Linux the menu is at the top right; on Android and phones it's in Settings → Language. English stays the default.
News, recaps and anything else new are translated too (with Google Translate). Product names and prices stay as they are.

My price-drop alerts: add the parts you're looking for in Prices → Price alerts and get told when their price goes down (any drop, or 5%, 10% or 20%). Turn it on in Settings → Notifications; it's off by default.
Laptop graphics chips are now called "Laptop GPU" instead of "Mobile" (just "Laptop" on phones).

title: The Benchmarking Update
notes: New Benchmarks tab in PC Hardware, between Compare and Buy or wait?: a ranking of about 80 graphics cards and 50 processors by gaming performance, with search and a filter by maker.
Bottleneck checker: pick your processor, graphics card and resolution (1080p, 1440p or 4K) to see which part limits your frame rate, about how many fps you get, and what to upgrade.

Buy or wait? has two new tabs. "Is this a good deal?": type the part and the price you were offered (new or used, in your currency) and get a verdict, with faster options for less money. "Used prices": what older graphics cards and processors are fairly worth second-hand.

Android: notifications while the app is closed. About every 15 minutes the app checks for new recaps, price drops, tracked items hitting your target and news matching your keywords, plus the morning summary. Turn it on or off in Settings → Notifications.
The app version is now shown at the bottom left on Windows, Mac and Linux (click it to open Updates), and at the bottom of Settings on Android and the web app.

title: The Mobile App Update
notes: Hardware Tracker now runs on Mac, Linux, Android and iPhone, not just Windows.
Mac: a .dmg for Apple Silicon and one for Intel Macs. The app tells you when a new version is out and links the download (Mac apps can only update themselves with a paid Apple certificate).
Linux: an AppImage that updates itself, and a .deb for Debian, Ubuntu and Mint.
Android: an app (.apk) with the in-app reader, live news and everything else. The Updates page tells you when a new version is out.

iPhone, iPad and any browser: a web app at https://tasttycheese.github.io/Hardware-Tracker/ . Open it in Safari and tap Share → Add to Home Screen, and it opens like an app. News comes from a snapshot refreshed every 20 minutes.
Phones get a new layout: the menu is a tab bar at the bottom, and the page tabs scroll sideways.
"Start with Windows" is now "Start when you sign in", since it works on Mac too.

title: GPU core counts
notes: Graphics cards now show how many cores they have, named the way each maker does: CUDA cores for Nvidia, stream processors for AMD and shading units for Intel. Core count is also a column in the GPU list, so you can sort by it.

Nvidia cards show streaming multiprocessors (SMs), AMD cards show compute units (CUs) and Intel Arc cards show Xe cores. AMD and Intel counts were missing before and are now filled in. AMD's ray tracing units are labelled ray accelerators.

DirectX, OpenGL, Vulkan, OpenCL and Shader model are now labelled as versions, and "CUDA" is labelled "CUDA compute capability (version)", so they aren't mistaken for counts. Texture units (TMUs) and render output units (ROPs) got clearer names too.

title: Sticky table headers, full-article translation and a full fact check
notes: Wide tables (PC Hardware lists and Prices) now have a horizontal scroll bar at the top that stays on screen while you scroll down, so you can move sideways without a tilt wheel or Shift+scroll. The column headers (Name, Year, Type…) also stay at the top while you scroll.

Translated news now opens the whole article in English: the title and every paragraph are translated inside the reader, keeping names that can't be translated. "Open in browser" opens the translated page too, and "Show original" switches back.

Fact check of every category: 67,000+ products checked for duplicates and impossible specs. About 4,200 duplicate listings were removed, same-named products now show what sets them apart (for example "XFX Swift OC (Radeon RX 9060 XT, 16 GB, White, 290 mm)" or "ADATA Premier 16 GB (DDR3-1600, CL11, Blue)"), boost clocks below the base clock were removed, and recent Ryzen and Intel Core CPUs now show their real launch year instead of the architecture's year.

Hand-added products checked one by one against manufacturer pages, Wikipedia and big hardware sites, with corrections to chipsets (B840, B860, H810, X670, A320), capture cards (Elgato 4K X and 4K Pro), VR headsets (field of view, weight and refresh rate on Rift, Quest, Pimax, Pico, Vive and Steam Frame), microphones, mouse pads, routers, printers, drawing tablets, controllers, streaming gear (Stream Deck Mini price, RODECaster Pro II faders) and historical CPUs (transistor counts for the 4004, 8080, 6502, Pentium III Tualatin and Pentium D).

title: Chipsets, capture cards, water cooling, translated news and a security pass
notes: New PC Hardware categories: Chipsets (55 Intel and AMD desktop and workstation chipsets with socket, supported CPUs, memory, overclocking, PCIe generation for the graphics slot and M.2, chipset lanes and USB4/Thunderbolt), Capture cards, Custom water cooling (blocks, pumps, reservoirs, radiators, tubing, fittings, coolant) and AIO water coolers (1,293 coolers by radiator size).
CPU coolers now have a Type filter: Air or AIO liquid.
Buy or wait?: new Clear button, and a ☆ favorite on each item. Favorites stay at the top and are kept when you clear the list.
Headlines and Live news: new Nvidia drivers tab for GeForce driver releases and hotfixes.
News in other languages is translated to English automatically (with a "Translated from …" note and a link to the original). You can turn this off in Settings → News language.
Fact check: chipset, capture card, VR headset, peripheral, launch-price and calendar data checked against manufacturer pages and big hardware sites; a few years, prices and specs were corrected.

Security: Electron 45 with the latest security fixes, updated build tools and libraries, stricter link and navigation checks, all browser permission requests denied, safer settings handling, and network requests that never send cookies or credentials. No passwords, keys or tokens are stored in the app or its code.

title: The big one: Compare, Buy or wait?, Launch calendar and more
notes: PC Hardware → Compare: put up to 4 products side by side (hardware with hardware, peripherals with peripherals). The best value in every row is highlighted in green, and GPUs and CPUs also show performance, price and price per performance.

PC Hardware → Buy or wait?: pick anything you're thinking of buying and get a verdict (good time to buy, fair, or better to wait) with the reasons: its price history, the market trend, newer models, upcoming launches, sales and the news.
Favorites: star any product. Favorites are pinned to the top of the list, with a filter for favorites first, only favorites, or not pinned.
Family trees: open a GPU or CPU to see the same tier across generations (e.g. GTX 1070 Ti → RTX 3070 Ti → RTX 4070 Ti → RTX 5070 Ti) and how much faster each one got.
Price tracker: new price-to-performance column with a "best value" tag and a "Best price to performance" sort. Products without a shop price yet use their launch price (MSRP).
Overview → Launch calendar: upcoming launches, events and rumored dates with countdowns, kept up to date by the daily recap.
Live news keyword alerts: add words you care about. New matching headlines light up a 🔔 with a red badge on Overview and Live news, like notifications in a social app.
Save as image: export a comparison or the price table as a PNG.

title: Live filter counts, back / forward, add products to the price tracker
notes: Filter counts are live: the number next to each manufacturer, type or year shows how many products you'd get with your current search and other filters.
Mouse back / forward buttons (buttons 4 and 5), and Alt+← / Alt+→, move through the pages and products you opened.
Clicking the menu or tab you're already on takes you to its start page.
Peripherals have full specs: VR headsets now list display, resolution, refresh rate, field of view, tracking, weight and price.
New spec sheets for microphones, controllers and wheels, mouse pads, printers and 3D printers, routers, drawing tablets and streaming gear.
Price tracker: "+ Add products" lets you pick GPUs and CPUs from the catalog, or build a memory kit by type, speed (MT/s), size, latency and desktop or laptop.
Memory now shows its specs first (DDR5, 6000 MT/s, 2 × 16 GB) and has its own type, speed and capacity filters.
"My products" shows just the products you added. Ones not on the weekly price list yet can be requested with one click.
The weekly price list grows to 53 products (more GPUs, CPUs and memory kits by spec).

title: Sorting, search and a better price tracker
notes: PC Hardware: new sorts Most popular / Least popular (PCPartPicker ranking) and Most used / Least used (Steam hardware survey, for graphics cards and VR headsets).
Search now comes first: results must match both your search and your filters, best name matches are listed first, and you get a clear message plus a one-click fix when nothing matches.
The "All categories" button stays visible while you scroll.
Graphics chips and cards are now one section called "Graphics cards (GPUs)". VR headsets now have data.
GPU and CPU labels now read GPUs and CPUs across Overview, Live news, Archive, Price tracker and Price alerts.
Price tracker: filter by GPUs, CPUs, RAM or Other with counts, search products, and sort by highest or lowest change, most recent or oldest change, or best deal vs MSRP.
Price tracker shows more: MSRP, change since the first price, lowest and highest price seen, number of data points, date of the last change, and a rising / falling summary.

title: PC Hardware improvements
notes: Updates now has its own place in the left menu, under Settings.
Graphics chips and retail graphics cards are one section, with a Type filter.
Retail graphics cards show the full specs of their GPU chip.
Categories and every filter list are in alphabetical order.
The search bar, filters and the product panel (with its close button) stay visible while you scroll.
More specs: CPU socket, process, memory and PCIe support; motherboard chipset, memory type and Wi-Fi; monitor pixel density and resolution class; SSD protocol.
Every product has a link to its full spec page online.

title: Updates page
notes: New Updates tab under Settings: see your version, what the next update adds, and how far the download is.
"Restart and update" button to install a downloaded update right away.
New checkbox to choose: install updates automatically when you quit, or only when you click Restart.
The update notification now opens the Updates tab.

title: PC Hardware section
notes: New PC Hardware section (between Prices and Settings) with Hardware and Peripherals tabs.
About 70,000 products in 38 categories: GPU chips since 1986, graphics cards, CPUs, motherboards, RAM, SSDs, hard drives, PSUs, coolers, cases, monitors, keyboards, mice, headsets and more.
Search and filter by manufacturer, year range and category specs; click a product for its full specifications.
The catalog updates itself twice a week and works offline once a category has been opened.

title: Tray mode, tracking and auto-updates
notes: New menu: Today, Overview, Prices and Settings, with tabs along the top.
Tracking tab: watch products with a target price and get notified when they hit it.
Runs quietly in the tray, starts with Windows, and closes itself when the PC is busy.
Daily and weekly recaps download automatically from GitHub every hour.
Installs from a setup file and updates itself.
